name: Led Zeppelin
hook: A band that borrowed heavily from American blues, lost or settled several cases over it, and whose drummer's sound became one of hip-hop's great breaks.
blurb: Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones and John Bonham formed Led Zeppelin in London in 1968. Their music was loud and heavy, built on American blues songs, and they are the sampling story from both sides. They drew heavily on American blues records and were challenged over it again and again: Willie Dixon's claim over 'Whole Lotta Love' was settled out of court in 1987, a claim over 'Dazed and Confused' was settled in 2012, and the long-running 'Stairway to Heaven' case was decided in the band's favour, upheld on appeal in 2020. Then hip-hop producers sampled them. 'When the Levee Breaks' (1971), itself a reworking of a 1929 blues by Kansas Joe McCoy and Memphis Minnie, has Bonham's drums recorded at the bottom of a stairwell in an old house called Headley Grange, with the microphones far above, so they sound enormous and echoing; Page's own accounts are the source for that. In 1986 the Beastie Boys looped those drums for 'Rhymin & Stealin'. The band ended in 1980 when Bonham died.
